localBiteReport: The most current dated report available is the Great Days Outdoors Northwest Florida Fishing Report for September 4–10, 2026 (roughly two weeks ago). According to that report, Choctawhatchee Bay is entering an early fall transition: baitfish schools — primarily greenies and menhaden — are pushing out of open water and concentrating in bayous, flats, bridge areas, and tidal roll-downs, which is steadily improving the bay's overall inshore bite. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters noted that redfish and general flats activity are expected to pick up further as September progresses into October, with slot-sized reds becoming increasingly available. A FishingBooker charter feed entry from Freeport dated August 6, 2026 noted that fish were biting best at first light through about 8:30 a.m. and again in the late afternoon from 5:00 p.m. to dark, with live menhaden on a Carolina rig producing well for redfish. Water temperature at this location is 86°F (same-day measured reading). Note: the most recent field reports found are approximately 1–2 weeks old; no same-week Choctawhatchee Bay inshore reports were located.
